Sea surface pH validation using gridded observations from ZISSOU¶

Matchup procedure: The model and observations were matched up as follows. First, the model dataset was cropped by a small amount to make sure cells close to the boundary were removed. The model was then regridded to the observational grid using bilinear remmaping. Only grid cells with model and observational data were maintained. The following model output was used to compare with the observational values: ph.

Baseline climatologies of sea surface pH¶

Climatologies of model and observational sea surface pH are shown in the figures below. The model climatology is calculated using the years 2000-2004.

Figure 1: Annual average surface pH from the model (2000-2004) and observations. Data is limited to the 2nd and 98th percentile of the combined model and observational data. Arrows indicate that values can exceed the colorbar limits.

Assessing model bias for surface pH¶

Figure 2 shows the average bias of surface pH simulated by the model. A positive bias indicates that the model overestimates the observation, while a negative bias indicates that the model overpredicts the observation.

The spatial average bias of surface pH is -0.01 1. Overall, the model underestimates the observations in 87.2% of the model domain.

Figure 2: Bias of surface pH from the model. A positive bias indicates that the model overestimates the observation. For clarity, the colorbar is limited to the 2nd and 98th percentile of the data.

Can the model reproduce spatial patterns of sea surface sea water pH?¶

The ability of the model to reproduce spatial patterns of sea surface pH was assessed by comparing the modelled and observed pH at each grid cell. We calculated the Pearson correlation coefficient between the modelled and observed pH at each grid cell.

This was carried out monthly and using the annual mean in each grid cell
